name: ALADInO
full_name: Antimatter Large Acceptance Detector In Orbit
summary: ALADInO is a high-acceptance space antimatter-detection proposal for deployment near Sun–Earth L2; the final mission orbit awaits approval. No launch date is confirmed, and design performance must not be presented as observational results.
detection_principle: A high-acceptance superconducting magnetic spectrometer separates matter from antimatter, combining particle identification and calorimetry to extend high-energy antiparticle spectra and distinguish dark-matter, pulsar and propagation explanations.

science_scope: Searches cosmic gamma-ray, antiparticle or neutrino spectra, directions and fluxes for indirect signatures of dark-matter annihilation, decay or related new physics. Conventional astrophysical sources and propagation can produce similar signals, requiring background modeling; design sensitivity is not a measured limit or discovery.
